title: Components and JSX
intro: React lets you build user interfaces from small, reusable pieces called components. In this lesson, you will learn how components, JSX, props, lists, conditional rendering, and composition fit together to build real interfaces.
takeaways: React applications are built by composing reusable function components that return JSX.
JSX looks like HTML but follows JavaScript-oriented rules such as className, camelCase attributes, closing tags, and expressions inside braces.
Props let a parent component pass data into a child component so the same component can render different content.
Use map to render lists and give each item a stable key so React can identify items correctly between renders.
Conditional rendering with && and ternaries lets components display different UI based on their data.

quiz.question: What is a React component?
options: A CSS file that controls a page
A JavaScript function that can return UI
A special type of database table
An HTML document that must contain a body element
quiz.explanation: A function component is a JavaScript function that returns React UI, usually written using JSX.

quiz.question: Which JSX code correctly assigns a CSS class?
options: Hello
Hello
Hello
Hello
quiz.explanation: JSX uses className rather than class for CSS classes because JSX attributes follow JavaScript-oriented naming conventions.

quiz.question: What does the key prop help React do when rendering a list?
options: It applies a CSS class to every list item
It prevents JavaScript from running
It identifies list items between renders
It automatically sorts the list
quiz.explanation: Keys give React a stable identity for items in a list, helping it understand which items were added, removed, or changed between renders.

quiz.question: What will this component render when showAdmin is false?
options:
function Panel({ showAdmin }) { return
{showAdmin && }
; }
A button containing the text Admin
The text false
An empty div with no Admin button
quiz.explanation: With && conditional rendering, the button is rendered only when showAdmin is truthy. When it is false, the expression does not render the button.

quiz.question: What values are passed to ProfileCard here?
options: <ProfileCard name="Anna" role="Developer" />
One prop called profile containing both values
Two props: name with value Anna and role with value Developer
No props because strings cannot be passed to components
quiz.explanation: The component receives two props: name and role. A component can use those values through its props parameter or by destructuring them.

exercise.title: Build reusable profile cards
exercise.task: Create a React function component called `ProfileCard` that accepts `name`, `role`, and `skills` as props. It must render an `article` with class `profile-card`, containing an `h2` with the name and a `p` with class `role` containing the role. When skills contains items, render a `ul` with one `li` per skill and give each list item a stable key; when skills is empty, render a `p` with class `no-skills` containing exactly `No skills yet` instead of the `ul`. Create an `App` component that renders two ProfileCard components: Anna, whose role is `Frontend developer` and whose skills are `React` and `CSS`, and Bence, whose role is `Backend developer` and whose skills array is empty. The exercise environment already provides React and ReactDOM globally, so do not use imports; `App` will be rendered automatically into `#root` before the tests run.
exercise.hint: Use a ternary expression to choose between the skills list and the empty-state paragraph. Render the skills array with map and use the skill value as the key because the exercise contains unique skill names. Then compose the two cards inside App.
